cards.front: Recall a key point about Power & Energy in Circuits
cards.back: Electrical power P = VI, measured in watts (W); 1 W = 1 J/s.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power & Energy in Circuits
cards.back: Using Ohm's Law, power can also be expressed as P = I²R or P = V²/R.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power & Energy in Circuits
cards.back: Electrical energy E = Pt, measured in joules (J); domestic energy is billed in kWh.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power & Energy in Circuits
cards.back: Resistors dissipate power as heat; this must be within the resistor's power rating to avoid damage.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power & Energy in Circuits
cards.back: Battery capacity is measured in amp-hours (Ah); a 2000 mAh battery can deliver 2 A for 1 hour.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power & Energy in Circuits
cards.back: Efficiency = useful power output / total power input, expressed as a percentage.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power & Energy in Circuits
cards.back: Energy lost as heat reduces efficiency; minimizing resistance in conductors reduces waste.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power & Energy in Circuits
cards.back: The total power supplied by a source equals the sum of power dissipated in all components.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power & Energy in Circuits
cards.back: Fuses are rated by current; they melt when power dissipation causes excessive temperature.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power & Energy in Circuits
cards.back: In AC circuits, power factor affects the real power delivered: P_real = VI cos φ.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power & Energy in Circuits
cards.back: A battery's internal resistance causes a voltage drop under load, reducing useful power output.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power & Energy in Circuits
cards.back: Energy conservation: energy supplied = energy stored + energy dissipated as heat.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse electronics exam tips — power & energy in circuits?
cards.back: 1. For Power & Energy in Circuits questions, use correct electronic symbols and terminology 2. Always show your working in calculations, including units at each step 3. When analysing circuits, state which law or rule you are applying first 4. For evaluation questions on Power & Energy in Circuits, compare component choices and consider cost, reliability and tolerance 5. Draw circuit diagrams neatly with conventional symbols
Explain the relationship between power, voltage, current and resistance in a circuit, and discuss how energy efficiency is affected by internal resistance.

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of power & energy in circuits, including electronic components, circuit theory and systems concepts relevant to WJEC Eduqas C690QS. AO2 (Application): Apply knowledge and understanding of power & energy in circuits to analyse, design and construct electronic circuits and systems. AO3 (Evaluation): Evaluate electronic circuits
